global.explain: Bytes InnoDB read from its data files (Innodb_data_read).
global.label: Data read

global.explain: Bytes InnoDB wrote (Innodb_data_written). On MySQL this includes redo log writes.
global.label: Data written

global.explain: Read operations on InnoDB data files (Innodb_data_reads); one can read several pages.
global.label: Read operations

global.explain: Redo log bytes (Innodb_os_log_written). MySQL re-counts rewrites of partly filled blocks, so it overstates a little.
global.label: Redo written

global.explain: Buffer pool pages read from disk (Innodb_buffer_pool_reads + Innodb_buffer_pool_read_ahead).
global.label: Pages read from disk

notes: Table figures are row operations through the storage engine (rows fetched, inserted, updated, deleted) and their time, which includes the file I/O inside each call. They are not bytes; the files show bytes.
Temporary and deleted files leave the per-file list when closed; their I/O stays in the file kinds, so check those for sort and temporary table spills.
InnoDB asynchronous I/O (read-ahead, page cleaner writes) is timed only for submitting the request: bytes are right, latency is understated.
Tables are limited to schema mfshop; files are server-wide.
Since server start covers 40 min 31 s of uptime.
